description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed by JSON) from the JSON machine-code study (fz vs BEAM JIT, lldb single-step traces). Study files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/ebbfffd8-2561-4da7-bcda-f9a316d00a1e/scratchpad/jsonasm/ (listings/, listings/beam/, CLIF dumps).

Evidence: 6-8 stp/ldp pairs plus moves into callee-saved registers, even in a 23-instruction leaf: 12-16 instructions per call. BEAM never saves them in the callee. Concordant: Make Distiller Fast's byte-walk hunt (develop 1438c8bfa) found each byte crossing dispatch and __clause_0, each pushing and popping five register pairs in series (~10 cycles per function), the saved registers used only on the yield path; Cranelift 0.137 (#711) left the saves unchanged (292 stp on g-spin).

Hypothesis (unconfirmed): the inlined yield slow path uses many registers and Cranelift does not shrink-wrap.

Done when: a probe moves the yield slow path to a cold out-of-line stub and counts prologue instructions before and after on the JSON leaves; reports a confirmed or refuted cause; proposes a fix only if confirmed. Re-measure on fz-sc8.247 (clause bodies become blocks).

comments.text: Callables (2026-11-17, continuation-cost study): prologue saves are 34 of 173 instructions in JSON's non-tail-call listing; a resume that uses two of five saved pairs spends 12 instructions on them.

Re-measured on merged fz-sc8.247 (MDF, 2eff1dec2): in the walk probe the five callee-saved pairs are saved once per call and the loop runs inside the function, so the per-turn save is gone for self-recursive loops. It remains for a leaf called once per item from another function; scope narrowed to that (title updated).

Contradicts the 2026-11-18 narrowing (Bugs and Cleanup, develop with fz-sc8.247 merged). Non-tail self-recursion still saves callee-saved registers at every level. sum(n) = n + sum(n-1) allocates its continuation, then branches 'b _fz_fn_23_sum__e23' to the function ENTRY, not to a loop block. So each level runs the x29/x30 frame and saves x19/x20/x22: 8 instructions and 6 memory operations. fz_op_add_ii saves x19/x20/x22 only for its overflow slow path.

Folded into fz-yh5.2 (user approved Callables' yh5.1/.2 page, 2026-11-24). Make Distiller Fast's measurement confirmed the cause (inlined yield slow path); the fix is yh5.2's out-of-line yield stub. Closes with fz-yh5.2's commit.

title: Measure why a native leaf called once per item saves x19-x28
